title: Bioluminescent Reagent Brewing Station
description: The user operates a chemistry lab workstation where a coffee mug serves as a mixing beaker and a lantern acts as a Bunsen-burner-style heat source. The user must drag reagent capsules into the mug in the correct order, ignite the lantern to the proper intensity, heat the mixture, and monitor a temperature gauge to synthesize a glowing bioluminescent compound without overheating.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive bioluminescent reagent brewing station. Load coffeeMug.glb and place it on a lab bench surface at center-right, scaled to act as a mixing beaker with a faint liquid plane inside that changes color as reagents are added. Load Lantern.glb and place it to the left beneath the mug, acting as an adjustable heat source; attach a PointLight to the lantern whose intensity and color the user controls. Camera: perspective at (0, 3, 5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to 45-degree vertical arc. Add a dark lab environment with subtle ambient light (0x1a1a2e) and a spotlight on the bench. Interaction steps (6-8): (1) Click a shelf panel to select Reagent-A capsule (blue sphere) and drag it into the mug — liquid turns blue. (2) Select Reagent-B (green sphere) and drag it in — liquid turns teal. (3) Click the lantern to ignite it — the PointLight activates with a flame-colored glow and a subtle flicker animation using sin-based intensity oscillation. (4) Use a slider UI element to adjust lantern heat intensity between 1 and 10; the PointLight intensity and color shift from orange to white accordingly. (5) Hold heat between 6-8 for 3 seconds — a temperature gauge (HTML overlay bar) must stay in the green zone; outside this range it turns red and the mixture destabilizes. (6) Once heated correctly, add Reagent-C (yellow sphere) — the liquid emits a bright bioluminescent glow using an emissive material with bloom via UnrealBloomPass from three/addons. (7) Click a 'Collect Sample' button to complete the task — the mug tilts with a tween animation pouring glowing liquid into a test tube. Validate each step: reagents must be added in order A-B-C, lantern must be lit before heating, temperature must be in range before adding C. Display step instructions in an HTML overlay panel. Use raycasting for drag-and-drop interactions. Add particle effects (small BufferGeometry points) rising from the mug when heated.
